Not allowed: AI writing a first draft of a manuscript or any section, AI creating or concluding the argument of an article, AI conducting a whole literature review or producing a whole reference list, and AI generating or manipulating research data or interview content. Allowed with disclosure: language editing (spelling, grammar, formatting, flow), suggesting references that the author verifies, idea generation, visualising data. Correction to the previous version: it rated leniency 3 and described AI as allowed for idea generation and language; the policy also forbids AI drafting and AI-built arguments, which weighs heavily for an argument-driven philosophy journal, so leniency is lowered to 2 |

## Format

Source for this section: the journal's Instructions for authors, read through the Wayback snapshot of 2025-06-30 (https://web.archive.org/web/20250630172041/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=sinq20; the live page returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-23; the snapshot's own text is dated "Updated 9th of June 2023"). Facts below are what the snapshot literally says; rules may have changed since.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research articles, symposia, special issues, target articles, review essays and critical discussions; unsolicited manuscripts are accepted (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/sinq20/about-this-journal, snapshot 2026-10-17). The instructions snapshot of 2025-06-30 is narrower: "Inquiry accepts the following types of article: original articles"; the two pages are not reconciled. The journal publishes only in English (instructions for authors, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-30) |
| **Word limit** | "There are no word limits for papers in this journal"; authors are asked to include a word count (instructions for authors, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-30) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Not applicable as stated: the snapshot sets no word limit (instructions for authors, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-30) |
| **Abstract limit** | The checklist says the paper "should contain an unstructured abstract of 200 words" (whether 200 is a maximum is not stated); a graphical abstract and a video abstract are optional; between 3 and 6 keywords (instructions for authors, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-30) |
| **Reference limit** | No numeric limit stated. Authors are told to use a Taylor & Francis reference guide (PDF at https://files.taylorandfrancis.com/tf_f.pdf, not opened, so the style name is not recorded here). House style: British (-ise) spelling, single quotation marks, quotations of 50 words or more indented, numbers one to nine spelled out (instructions for authors, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-30) |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed; published online via Figshare. Data: the journal applies the Taylor & Francis Basic Data Sharing Policy, under which sharing and citing data and giving a Data Availability Statement are encouraged, not required. Disclosure-of-interest statement and funding details are required in the checklist. Authorship follows the Taylor & Francis authorship criteria, affiliations are those where the research was conducted, and the affiliation cannot be changed after acceptance. Review model: after the editor's suitability check, double anonymous review by two independent referees. Fees: "no submission fees, publication fees or page charges"; open access is optional through Open Select with an article publishing charge (amount not stated in the snapshot); print colour figures carry a charge (instructions for authors, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-30) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit stated. Figures at 1200 dpi for line art, 600 dpi for grayscale and 300 dpi for colour, in EPS, PS, JPEG, GIF or Word; tables should present new information and be supplied in editable form; manuscripts may be submitted in Word, with templates available; required order: title page, abstract, keywords, main text, acknowledgments, declaration of interest, references, appendices, tables, figures, captions (instructions for authors, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-30) |

### Orientation

> Keyword counts below are from Crossref records for ISSN 0020-174X, journal articles dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 886 records, of which 0 carry a deposited abstract. Matching was therefore done on TITLES ONLY, locally, retrieved 2026-11-23. Titles are a much thinner text than abstracts, so every count is a strong lower bound and a low score reflects the thinness of titles as much as the journal. Percentages use the 886 titles. Recent titles in the Crossref pull (2026) fit that: democracy and science (DOI 10.1080/0020174x.2026.2755743), game-theoretic analysis of AI governance (10.1080/0020174x.2026.2757100), procreation and moral reasons (10.1080/0020174x.2026.2759723), talking with language models (10.1080/0020174x.2026.2745114). **Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** conceptual and argumentative philosophy; symposia, target articles, review essays and critical discussions (listed on the about page); formal and game-theoretic argument appears in titles; philosophy of AI and language models.

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

- Scope statement: the about page says the journal publishes "in all areas of philosophy" and offers a forum for "a variety of perspectives"; it states no school or political line (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/sinq20/about-this-journal, snapshot 2026-10-17).
- Named thinkers in titles of 886 articles, 2021-2026 (Crossref titles only, retrieved 2026-11-23): Nietzsche 23 (2.6%), Kant 18 (2.0%), Frege or Russell 7 (0.8%), Aristotle 6 (0.7%), Hegel 5 (0.6%), Heidegger 5 (0.6%), Hume 2 (0.2%), Rawls 2 (0.2%), Wittgenstein 1 (0.1%), Marx 0.
- Topic vocabulary in titles: "knowledge|epistem*|belief|testimony" 99 (11.2%), "moral|ethic*" 58 (6.5%), "language|meaning|semantic" 39 (4.4%), "metaphys*|modal|essence|grounding|causation" 36 (4.1%), "free will|agency|action" 34 (3.8%), "pragmat*" 11 (1.2%), "phenomen*" 8 (0.9%), "feminis*|gender" 6 (0.7%).
- OpenAlex topics (spine, 2026-07-13): Philosophy and Theoretical Science 764 articles, Epistemology, Ethics, and Metaphysics 726, Philosophical Ethics and Theory 468, Philosophy and History of Science 382.
- Editorial board names listed on the about page include John Hawthorne, Susanna Siegel, Øystein Linnebo, Stewart Shapiro, John Broome and Rae Langton (snapshot 2026-10-17).
- Reading of the counts: titles are dominated by epistemology, ethics, language and metaphysics vocabulary, while continental vocabulary (Hegel, Heidegger, phenomenology) each stays under 1% of titles. This describes what is published, not an editorial stance; titles cannot show method or politics.

### Framing Requirements

- Mandatory framing: none stated; scope is "all areas of philosophy" and regular issues accept submissions in all areas (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/sinq20/about-this-journal, snapshot 2026-10-17).
- Article types: research articles, symposia, special issues, target articles, review essays and critical discussions; unsolicited manuscripts accepted (same page).
- Gatekeeping: every submission gets an initial appraisal by the Editor before any peer review; the publisher states a 9-day median to first decision including desk rejections and a 17% acceptance rate for the last full calendar year (same page).
- Title form in 886 titles (Crossref, 2021-2026): 215 (24.3%) contain a colon and 97 (10.9%) a question mark, so a stated-thesis or question-led title is common.
- Consequence of ignoring the scope: not stated on the pages read (about page snapshot 2026-10-17; instructions snapshot 2025-06-30).

### Methodological Preferences

Scoring rule (this pass's own convention, not a journal statement): hits divided by the 886 records; because Crossref holds no abstracts for this journal, hits are counted in titles only, so every score is a floor. 0 gives 0, under 1% gives 1, 1-5% gives 2, over 5% gives 3. Scores of 4-5 need an editorial statement and none was found. Source: Crossref titles for ISSN 0020-174X, 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23.

### Voice & Style

- Title form: 215 of 886 titles (24.3%) carry a colon and 97 (10.9%) a question mark (Crossref, 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Ten most recent titles sampled (Crossref, 2026): a mix of argued-thesis and topic titles, for example "Disagreement and trust: the case from democracy and science" (DOI 10.1080/0020174x.2026.2755743), "Procreation and moral reasons: balancing prerogatives and harm" (10.1080/0020174x.2026.2759723), "Strong AI and the method of explication" (10.1080/0020174x.2026.2748284) and "Talking with language models" (10.1080/0020174x.2026.2745114); two are discussions of a named author's book or work ("Ori Beck on reformed empiricism", 10.1080/0020174x.2026.2751143).
- Abstract limit and house style: an unstructured abstract of 200 words, British (-ise) spelling and single quotation marks are stated in the instructions snapshot of 2025-06-30 (see Format). First-person use and the citation style name are not determined: Crossref holds 0 abstracts for the 886 records, so no abstract or article opening could be inspected, and the reference-guide PDF was not opened.

### Practical Concerns

- Anonymisation: all peer review is double anonymised (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/sinq20/about-this-journal, snapshot 2026-10-17).
- Submission route: ScholarOne at mc.manuscriptcentral.com/inquiry; the journal states it accepts only manuscripts submitted through that service (same page).
- AI: authors must disclose generative-AI use; AI may not draft sections or build the argument (https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/editorial-policies/using-ai-in-your-research-and-manuscript-preparations/, read 2026-11-23).
- Preprints and archiving: pre-submission preprints are allowed; accepted-manuscript embargo for social sciences and humanities journals is stated as 18 months (https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/research-impact/sharing-versions-of-journal-articles/, read 2026-11-23); the journal-specific embargo was not read.
- OA and charges: hybrid, no APC unless open access is chosen (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/sinq20/about-this-journal, snapshot 2026-10-17); the APC amount was not read.
- Ethics and data (instructions snapshot 2025-06-30): research on humans or animals needs a Methods statement of approval by the relevant ethics committee, or, where no formal committee exists, a statement that the study follows the Declaration of Helsinki; participant consent is required; the Basic Data Sharing Policy encourages data sharing and a Data Availability Statement; authorship follows the Taylor & Francis criteria. Independent-scholar rules: not stated on the snapshot (it asks only for the affiliation where the research was conducted).

## Strategic Notes

> Every statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Judgements about the journal's culture are not made because the evidence for them is absent.

### Hard Blockers

- A non-anonymised manuscript: all peer review is double anonymised (Peer Review table).
- Work the editor finds out of scope or unsuitable: every manuscript gets an initial editor appraisal and the publisher reports a 17% acceptance rate (Framing Requirements, Metrics).
- Generative-AI drafting of text or of the argument: the T&F policy forbids it (AI Policy table).

### Soft Tax

- Disclosure statement for any generative-AI use, including tool name and version (AI Policy table).
- A posted preprint can reveal identity to reviewers of a double-anonymised journal (Preprint table); no journal rule on this was read.
- Format rules come from an instructions snapshot of 2025-06-30 (no word limit, a 200-word unstructured abstract, 3 to 6 keywords, British spelling) and may have changed; re-read the live instructions page before submitting (Format table). The citation style name is not recorded.

### Best Suited For

- General argumentative philosophy in epistemology, ethics, language and metaphysics: these terms appear in 4-11% of titles each (Orientation, Epistemological Leanings).
- Philosophy of AI and language models: 12 titles with "language model|ChatGPT|LLM" and 25 with AI terms (Sensitive Topics).
- Authors who value a fast first signal: the publisher states a 9-day median to first decision, though the 102-day figure applies once a paper goes to review (Review Cycle Time).

### Not Recommended For

- Empirical, qualitative or quantitative studies: such terms appear in 0.1-0.7% of titles (Methodological Preferences); this is rarity in titles, not a stated exclusion.
- Work needing a high acceptance probability: the publisher-stated acceptance rate is 17% (Metrics).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Pacific Philosophical Quarterly](./pacific-philosophical-quarterly.md) | In the corpus; its entry records mainstream analytic philosophy across core subfields, see that entry for its own data |
| 2 | [Canadian Journal of Philosophy](./canadian-journal-of-philosophy.md) | In the corpus; its entry records a general analytic journal open to any area, see that entry |
| 3 | [European Journal of Philosophy](./european-journal-of-philosophy.md) | In the corpus; its entry records work spanning analytic and continental traditions, see that entry |

*(Fit reasoning is limited to the scope sentences in the entries named; acceptance odds are not estimated.)*
